correctness.rationale: For two distinct q-ary Hamming words the intersection of exact-distance-one neighborhoods has size q-2, 2 or 0 as their distance is 1, 2 or at least 3. This yields k-2 <= max(q-2,2). In a k>=5 scale pairwise attributes are adjacent, forcing them onto a coordinate line; every object must then lie on that line and equal its matched attribute. At k=4, three objects adjacent to a designated attribute can vary in precisely one, two, or three coordinate directions; the three exhaustive cases force respectively a full line (q=4), two parallel two-point lines with four distinct symbols (q=4), or one parity class of a binary 3-face (q=2,3,4). Each has unique witnesses. Direct disjoint-coordinate counting gives the formulas and the d<=2 exceptions. Reproducibility: python3 verify.py exhaustively checks 4,321,392 support candidates in 14 parameter pairs and 25,000 sampled five-support cases; this is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Maximum contranominal dimension is a natural concept-lattice Boolean-suborder invariant, not an arbitrary subfamily. The theorem explains why the q=4 transition produces three intrinsically distinct geometric extremizers and gives complete enumerations for every nontrivial large-arity regime. For q>=5, the invariant diverges linearly with alphabet size while the open-neighborhood VC dimension remains bounded by three, a meaningful nonimplication between central FCA and model-theoretic complexity measures. These claims require structural rigidity beyond the standard intersection lemma and offer reusable exact benchmark families.
